source_intents.action_description: Log in as a newly onboarded Primary User, navigate to checkout, add a credit card if prompted, and submit an order
source_intents.expected_behavior: Checkout completes successfully; order is submitted and user is redirected to the order confirmation screen
preconditions: iOS Case has been submitted and SF Case ID exists
Location is Active or Inactive with an approved payment method
test_data_hints: Primary user with iOS SF Case ID present in Salesforce
No NAV ID on the account
Valid credit card for payment entry
source_intents.original_text: CF-01 | Immediate Checkout After Onboarding | Smoke | Simulated Checkout Post-Onboarding-eligibility | Primary User; iOS Case submitted (SF Case ID exists); Payment Status = Approved; No NAV ID; Company = Approved; Location = Active or Inactive with approved payment method | 1. Login as the user 2. Proceed to checkout 3. Add credit card if prompted 4. User enters the CC and submits orders

source_observations.summary: Primary user login — returns JWT token successfully
Get customer profile — confirms no NAV ID, IOS case present, payment approved
Set shipping information — Standard delivery selected
Place order with qty=1 (below MOQ=2) — order ACCEPTED, MOQ check did not fire

reconciliation.reasoning: OBS-001 confirms login succeeds for a Primary user with iOS case and Approved payment status. OBS-002 confirms no NAV ID on the account. OBS-008 confirms order placement returns HTTP 200 with a valid order_id. The full onboarding-to-checkout flow matches the intent.
reconciliation.final_expected_behavior: Checkout completes successfully; order is submitted and user is redirected to the order confirmation screen

classification.reasoning: Behavior spans an HTTP POST controller that returns JSON — API level is the right fit. Unit testing OnboardingProcess::execute() would require mocking the entire Magento DI graph. E2E would be too brittle for this smoke check.

alternatives_considered.reason_rejected: Would require mocking the Magento DI container, ObjectManager, and session — integration value too low relative to mocking cost.
Browser automation overhead unjustified for a single POST endpoint smoke check; E2E reserved for full user flows.

alternatives_rejected.draft_summary: Initial draft omitted the group_id fallback path entirely.
alternatives_rejected.reason_rejected: Save.php line 80-82 implements a critical fallback when group_id is absent; a test that ignores it has low coverage delta.

dimensions.name: syntactic_validity
dimensions.notes: Valid PHP throughout. Correct TestCase extension, proper Guzzle Client instantiation, type declarations are consistent.

dimensions.name: behavior_fidelity
dimensions.notes: Covers the unauthenticated redirect (Save.php line 70-73), the JSON response structure, and the end-to-end checkout flow. Missing: does not assert that the order confirmation response contains a non-null order_id from NAV (nav_order_id), which is part of the agreed expected behavior.

dimensions.name: coverage_delta
dimensions.notes: Adds new coverage for the onboarding save controller and the post-login checkout path. The group_id fallback test (testMissingGroupIdFallsBackToCustomerGroup) exercises Save.php line 80-82, which would otherwise have no API-level test.

dimensions.name: assertion_quality
dimensions.notes: assertArrayHasKey('success') is good. testCheckoutSucceedsAfterOnboarding asserts assertIsInt and assertGreaterThan(0) on orderId — specific and correct. Weakness: testOnboardingPostReturnsJsonWithSuccessKey does not assert the value of the 'success' key (true vs false).

dimensions.name: determinism
dimensions.notes: No random values or clock dependencies. All test data comes from env vars. Minor risk: testCheckoutSucceedsAfterOnboarding leaves an order in the system — add a tearDown to cancel or the next run may see unexpected cart/order state.

steering_signals_applied.rule_text: Always cite source file and line number in test method docblock for traceability.
Prefer assertSame over assertEquals for HTTP status code assertions (strict type safety).
